en: The Sūtra of the Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī. This sūtra is extracted from the *Mahāpadma-vajrasamaya-adhiṣṭhāna-guhyāpratihatadhāraṇī-sūtra*.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Tang Dynasty.
Part 1: The Introduction; Chapter One, the Introduction.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying on Mount Kailāsa together with an immeasurable assembly of bodhisattvas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat, adjusted his robes,
knelt with palms joined, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Bhagavān, I possess the Great Lotus Peak Vajra Secret Unobstructed Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī-vidyā-samaya,
which is capable [of accomplishing] all superior and meritorious activities."
"Whatever is sought shall all be attained as desired and accomplished.
Since the Tathāgata, in his great compassion, has granted me permission to speak,
I shall now rely upon the Buddha's spiritual power."
It was spoken for the sake of extensively benefiting the aspirations of all sentient beings.
World-Honored One, this dhāraṇī-mantra possesses great majestic power,
like a celestial wish-fulfilling tree.
For all the vidyādhara-sages, it rains down a great rain of jewels;
whatever they desire is obtained, equal to a maṇi-gem,
capable of fulfilling every supreme aspiration of all sentient beings.
"I only pray that the Tathāgata will compassionately grant his sustaining power.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! You possess great compassion."
For the sake of all sentient beings, you have asked this question.
I have empowered you to explain the vidyā-mantra of the Cintāmaṇicakra-dhāraṇī without obstruction.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—

circumambulated the Buddha three times, and returned to his original seat.
With a heart of joy,
he gazed intently at the assembly with a serene smile and then spoke the root dhāraṇī-mantra, saying:

When this dhāraṇī-mantra was being recited,
the great earth, its mountains and forests, shook in six ways; likewise,
all the palaces of the devas, the palaces of the nāgas, and the palaces of the yakṣas trembled.
The palaces of the rākṣasas, the palaces of the gandharvas,
the palaces of the asuras, the palaces of the garuḍas,
the palaces of the kiṃnaras, and the palaces of the mahoragas.
All were greatly shaken;
the various evil and powerful spirits, yakṣas,
and vināyakas who create obstacles were all struck with great terror.
Great fires broke out throughout all the palaces of the māras;
therein, the māra kings and their retinues were struck with great terror,
as were all the base and wicked nāgas, goddesses, and female spirits.
Female ghosts, yakṣīs, rākṣasīs, gandharvīs, asurīs, and garuḍīs.
The kinnara women and mahoraga women were simultaneously struck with terror and confusion, falling prostrate upon the ground;
the gates of all the hells opened of their own accord.
Within this, all sentient beings who were reaping the karmic retribution of their sins attained liberation;
at the end of their lives, they were reborn in the celestial realms to enjoy supreme peace and happiness.
At that time, the various devas each held various kinds of sublime *agaru* and ox-head sandalwood from the heavens.
Agalloch wood powder incense, unguents, and burning incense;
wondrous celestial flowers, various precious necklaces,
hairpins, earrings, bracelets, jeweled canopies, and crowns.
All manner of celestial garments and ornaments rained down in profusion from the void,
making offerings to the Tathāgata and the great assembly.
Filling the reaches of space, clouds of various colors arose;
from within those clouds, immeasurable celestial music played spontaneously without being struck,
producing inconceivable, harmonious, and elegant sounds as an offering to the Tathāgata.
Those who see, hear, or listen shall abide in the power of loving-kindness and patience.
Such spiritual transformations as these are all brought about by the supernatural power of the Secret Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī-mantra of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
At that time, the World-Honored One uttered the exquisite, Brahma-like voice of the kalaviṅka bird and spoke these profound and wondrous verses in praise of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara:
“Excellent, excellent, son of good family! That you are able to take pity upon all sentient beings.”
By reciting this *Cintāmaṇi-dhāraṇī*, which provides great and supreme benefit for the salvation of sentient beings,
those who believe and accept it shall eliminate all sins, transcend the three realms, and realize Bodhi.
Wherever there are those who practice and uphold it in any direction, their worldly and world-transcending aspirations shall all be fulfilled.
At that time, having spoken these verses, the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Good son, you should once more [expound this] for the sake of all sentient beings."
Having spoken this method for receiving and upholding the *ṛddhi-dhāraṇī* mantra, it shall cause sentient beings to obtain great and virtuous benefit.
**Chapter Two: On Destroying Karmic Obstructions from the *Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*** At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
if there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or boys and girls who, in this present life,
seek great merit as a reward in the present existence..."
One should diligently practice this *Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī* according to the Dharma day and night,
without depending on the selection of auspicious days, months, or constellations.
Furthermore, one should not fast for one or two days,
nor bathe, nor construct an altar; rather,
wearing ordinary clothes, one should purify oneself by sprinkling clear water.
As in the usual practice for the consecration rite using vegetarian food,
one should dwell in a pure chamber during the day and night, sitting cross-legged facing east and visualizing oneself as the body of Avalokiteśvara.
With the marks and signs of perfection complete like the rising sun,
emitting great radiance and seated upon a lotus flower,
he stands directly before one; recite his name with undistracted mind.
Burn aloeswood incense and offer it with a focused mind;
pay respectful homage according to what your heart provides,
presenting offerings of incense and flowers without interruption.
Recite one thousand and eighty times during each of the six periods of the day, continuing without interruption.
Recite each syllable three hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*—in Sanskrit; *shiwàn* in Chinese) while abiding in the yoga of meditative visualization.
All past and present offenses of the five immediate transgressions and extremely evil karmic obstructions will naturally be extinguished,
and one shall see various kinds of great auspicious dreams.
One should know that this is the sign of the extinction of transgressions;
through the empowerment and protective mindfulness of the Noble Avalokiteśvara,
by means of these roots of virtue, hundreds of thousands of activities [will be accomplished].
If one raises the mind to recite and remember it, all that one undertakes shall be fully accomplished.
Among all vidyās, supernatural powers, and majestic might,
none can equal the power of the vidyā and supernatural faculties of this *Cintāmaṇicakra-dhāraṇī*.
Why is this? If there are those who can faithfully accept and uphold this dhāraṇī, their accumulated offenses and obstructions from the four pārājikas,
the five heinous crimes, and the ten evil deeds committed in the past and present [shall be purified].
It can completely eliminate those who are destined to fall into the Avīci Hell; likewise,
it cures fevers and wind-related ailments for one day, two days, three days, four days, and even up to seven days.
Bilious fevers, phlegmatic illnesses, and the poisons of sorcery and malevolent incantations;
carbuncles, scabies, leprosy, epilepsy, and wind-induced itching;
ailments of the head, nose, eyes, ears, lips, tongue, and teeth.
All diseases of the throat, chest, ribs, heart, abdomen,
waist, back, hands, feet, limbs, and joints;
and all manner of calamities, malevolent spirits, and ghosts.
By reciting and chanting this sutra, all [obstacles] shall be eliminated.
No yakṣas, rākṣasas, vināyakas, malevolent spirits, ghosts,
or the like shall be able to cause harm.
May there be no mutual harm from the calamities of weapons, water, fire, evil winds, thunder, and hail;
nor from the perils of kings, thieves, or enemies.
May all inauspicious signs and karmic deeds resulting from meager merit be extinguished.
Malevolent stars and portents shall all naturally vanish;
venomous snakes, vipers, scorpions, lizards, spiders,
lions, tigers, wolves, and all other predatory beasts shall likewise not cause harm.
If one encounters military arrays, battles, official affairs, or disputes and litigation,
through the accomplishment of this illumination, one shall attain liberation from them all.
If one constantly recites this dhāraṇī one thousand and eighty times at the fifth watch of the night, [the same result shall be achieved].
Regarding all such matters as those mentioned above, one shall attain liberation, mastery, and the fulfillment of one's wishes.
If one can recite this dhāraṇī one thousand and eighty times during each of the six periods of the day, [the aforementioned results will be achieved].
The Noble Avalokiteśvara appeared to him in a dream upon his awakening, stood before that person, and said: "O son of noble family, do not fear!
Whatever wish you seek, I shall grant it all to you."
Some see Amitābha Buddha;
some see the world of Sukhāvatī and its magnificent palaces, towers, and pavilions.
In some instances, one sees the assembly of bodhisattvas in the world of Sukhāvatī;
in others, one sees all the assemblies of the Buddhas and bodhisattvas from the ten directions gathered together;
and in yet others, one sees the palace of seven treasures on Mount Potalaka where the noble Avalokiteśvara dwells.
Some see their own bodies, both internally and externally, purified;
some see kings and ministers respectfully making offerings to them;
and some see all the karmic obstacles of their past lives being completely extinguished.
It should be known that after such a person passes away, they will not undergo birth from a womb;
rather, they will be born by transformation within a lotus,
with a physical form that is upright and beautiful, adorned with celestial garments.
In every place of rebirth, they possess the wisdom of knowing past lives until they reach Bodhi;
they shall never again fall into the three evil realms,
and will always be in the company of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Abiding in the same place of birth, they dwell on the stage of non-retrogression.
Chapter Three: The Method for Recitation from the *Sūtra of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel Dhāraṇī*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
He addressed the Buddha again, saying: "World-Honored One,
this Secret Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī further possesses two dharmas."
First, that which pertains to the mundane world;
second, that which pertains to the supramundane world.
Regarding what is called "the mundane world":
This refers to the method of recitation and contemplation for the fulfillment of supreme vows;
through it, one achieves the conversion and guidance of sentient beings,
as well as the accomplishment of wealth, status, power, and majestic virtue.
That which is called "supramundane" refers to the adornment of the provisions of merit, wisdom, and liberation;
it involves the increase of compassion for sentient beings suffering in distress, and being loved and respected by all people.
This secret essence of the sūtra should be maintained in strict secrecy.
It must not be proclaimed to those who lack understanding.
If one realizes this secret samaya, [it shall be so].
You should keep this secret and not proclaim it recklessly.
If one truly accomplishes this most supreme dharma of the dhāraṇī,
then in all circumstances— whether eating or not eating, whether pure or impure— [one shall be liberated].
With single-minded concentration, visualize the holy Avalokiteśvara with all his physical marks and signs complete,
radiant like the sun at its rising;
recite this dhāraṇī without any distracted thoughts.
If one constantly maintains this practice without interruption and commits no transgressions,
then the Noble Avalokiteśvara will manifest his golden-hued body,
removing all defilements and obstacles through the empowerment of his divine power.
May all the aspirations of the mind be fulfilled.
May one realize the various supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) and the *āttadāna* dharmas,
as well as the dharma of great learning and upholding the teachings, and the wish-fulfilling gem (*cintāmaṇi*) dharma.
The method for the medicinal elixir of longevity; the method for raining down the jewels of the Dharma;
the method for beholding hidden treasures; the method for entering the caves of the asuras;
the method for assuming forms at will; and various methods for medicinal substances.
Through the rites of the ritual pestle and the ritual vase, all desired goals— both mundane and supramundane—
shall be accomplished. Should there be a king,
a queen, or a consort, [they shall likewise attain success].
Princes, princesses, and ministers;
brahmins, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras; bhikṣus, whether male or female, boys or girls; and all those who follow non-Buddhist paths.
Those who prostrate with faith and accept and uphold this Dharma should know the proper timing:
if a king recites it during seven days, [the results will be attained].
In each of the six periods of the day, one should recite it one thousand and eighty times.
If it is a consort or a queen, she should recite it nine hundred times in each period.
If it is a prince, he should recite it eight hundred times.
If a princess recites it seven hundred times;
if a minister recites it six hundred times;
if a Brahmin recites it five hundred times.
If a Kṣatriya recites it four hundred times;
if a Vaiśya recites it three hundred times;
and if a Śūdra recites it two hundred times.
If a bhikṣu recites it one hundred and eight times;
if a man recites it one hundred and six times;
if a woman recites it one hundred and three times.
If a young boy recites it one hundred times,
or if a young girl recites it ninety times,
this is called the method of daily practice (kē-fǎ).
By maintaining mindfulness and reciting the name, all supreme matters will be accomplished.
Wealth, nobility, blessings, happiness, provisions, grain, silks, servants, elephants, horses,
and all articles of enjoyment will increase according to one's wishes.
The wise person should, at all times, recite one thousand and eighty repetitions from the latter part of the night until the appearance of the dawn light,
never failing in this practice; thus, they shall achieve all boundless undertakings.
Within an area of one hundred yojanas, the gods, men,
and women will swiftly return to pay homage and offer praise, as fast as the wind;
if they wish, the noble Avalokiteśvara will appear and grant their aspirations.
Having purified oneself by bathing and anointed the body with powdered incense,
one should wear clean garments and consume the three white foods.
One should prepare, according to one's means, fragrant flowers and scented water.
Offer white foods, fruits, and melons;
blend agalloch incense, white sandalwood incense, and so forth with clarified butter and honey;
facing east, sit in the full lotus posture.
Visualizing the Noble Avalokiteśvara and reciting the Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī,
light one [wick] and burn it for one hundred thousand times;
then the Noble Avalokiteśvara will manifest his body and speech to fulfill all the aspirations of the practitioner of the vidyā-mantra.
If one wishes to cause the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha to appear,
one should blend aloeswood incense,安息香 (an-hsi-xiang), and other incenses with ghee and honey; then,
with single-minded clarity and a single thought, [one should invoke] the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha.
If one performs this burning incantation one hundred thousand times,
the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha will manifest his own form;
he who contemplates the vidyā-mantra will be cherished by him as a son.
One is granted the vessel of a vidyādhara for all [practices].
If one desires to cause all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to appear,
one should offer aloeswood incense while maintaining a single mantra and a single thought toward all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
If one performs this incense offering one hundred thousand times,
all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas will manifest their own bodies to remove obstacles and fulfill all requested aspirations.
If one wishes for all the great vidyādhara sages to appear,
one should burn agallochum incense mixed with ghee for seven days and seven nights; then,
in a single moment of clear awareness, the great vidyādhara sages will manifest.
After burning for seven full days and nights,
all the great Vidyādhara ṛṣis will manifest their own forms before this person and each present their vidyā-mantras to the practitioner.
He shall further bestow his divine power to follow and protect you.
If you wish for Śakra, the Lord of the Trichiliocosm, or Brahmā, together with their hosts of devas,
to appear, for seven days and seven nights, one should blend *agaru* incense, *kunduruka* incense, and other fragrances with clarified butter and honey.
First, it clarifies that in a single thought-moment, Śakra and Brahmā,
having burned for seven full days and nights,
[were joined] by Śakra, Brahmā, and the hosts of devas.
They all manifested their own bodies to preach the Dharma and offer consolation, protecting them in accordance with the vows they had made.
Chapter Four: The Seal of the Dharma (*Dharmamudrā-parivarta*). At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
He addressed the Buddha again, saying: "World-Honored One,
regarding this Secret Wish-Fulfilling Wheel Dhāraṇī, its vidyās, and mudrās,
they serve for protection, offering, invocation, welcoming, and dismissal."
One must certainly visualize clearly according to the ritual manual without any error;
then one will attain accomplishment in this secret samaya.
1. The Great Lotus Samaya Mudrā: For the Great Lotus Samaya Mudrā, join the palms of both hands together.
With the two index fingers, the two middle fingers, and the two ring fingers,
extend each upward and slightly bend them apart;
the tips of the index fingers should be one and a half inches apart.
The two thumbs and the two little fingers are each held upright, touching one another, and slightly bent.
The mantra for this mudrā is as follows:
Namo ratnatrayāya. Nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya. Oṃ maṇi padme hūṃ. Sarva-saṃskāra-parivartana-nu-ratna-nirukti svāhā. When one wishes to construct a maṇḍala:
On the site of the maṇḍala, one should first recite the Threefold Vidyā of Body and Mind one thousand and eighty times.
Then, having bound this mudrā and vidyā seven times,
one should brandish the mudrā three times each toward the east, south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and above and below.
With a calm mind, visualize a hundred-petaled or thousand-petaled lotus flower made of the seven precious gems in full bloom;
by making this offering, may all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, devas, nāgas, and spirits be filled with joy.
Whenever one wishes to bathe,
one should empower the water with the *vidyā* mantra and the syllable *hrīḥ*.
Reciting the mantra seven times over the water, one should rub it with the right hand and use it for bathing.
Not to be used when [the mind] is unclear.
2. The Seal of Liberation (Mudrā of Liberation), second: With the two little fingers and the two ring fingers, cross them within the palms, with the right hand pressing over the left.
The two middle fingers are held upright with their tips touching.
The two index fingers are each bent back against the backs of the middle fingers like hooks,
their tips positioned three finger-widths from the backs of the middle fingers.
Place the two thumbs side by side and erect them.
The mantra is as follows:
*Namaḥ mahāśriye oṃ śrīkari samaye svāhā siddhisiddhe svadhāye svāhā svāhā svāhā svāhā svāhā*. One should perform this mudrā and recite this mantra three times.
Place the mudrā upon the crown of the head, the shoulders, the heart, and the throat.
Having completed the protection of the body, encircle the garment with the mudrā;
this will cause all vināyakas [to be subdued].
Being far removed, it does not act as an obstruction and transcends all hindrances.
Furthermore, one should use this mudrā to protect all offering substances and the like,
and then present them in worship.
3. Purifying the Earth. The third section on purifying the earth: Oṃ [as before] bhuḥ va-ra-hūṃ. One should take pure earth and divide it into three portions.
Recite this clearly seven times over the earth.
With one portion, wash from the waist downward;
with another portion, wash from the shoulders upward. Repeat this seven times.
First, wash the head and neck.
(4) The Touching the Protective Body Seal, the fourth: join the two index fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers;
within the palms, cross them with the right over the left.
The tips of the two middle fingers are bent;
the backs of the nails of the two index fingers are joined together;
and the two thumbs are extended side by side.
Grasp the sides of the middle two fingernails.
The mudrā-mantra is:
Oṃ rudraṇa hūṃ cchaḥ. Having performed this mudrā and mantra three times, protect the body.
When going to various places of contact or to the latrine,
one should enter and exit as usual and perform the ritual cleansing.
Furthermore, one should go to a specific spot to take earth and wash the hands.
And for rinsing the mouth and cleaning the teeth. 5.
The Mudrā for Rinsing the Mouth (Mukha-śodhana-mudrā), fifth: With the right hand, the tips of the thumb, index, and middle fingers are slightly bent together;
the ring finger and little finger are bent like hooks.
The mudrā and mantra are as follows:
Oṃ dhu dhu ri kuru kuru svāhā. Having formed this mudrā, empower the water three times with the mantra.
Wash the mouth and teeth, and drink and sprinkle *śauca* water.
If you wish to bathe,
first bathe the Three Jewels.
Next, having bathed the Holy Avalokiteśvara, one bathes oneself. 6.
The Seal for Bathing the Triple Gem (Ṣaṣṭha): With both hands, palms facing upward, the sides are placed together.
Bend the two index fingers, each pressing against the upper part of the two thumbs.
Join the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers, extending them flatly.
The mantra for this mudrā is as follows:
Oṃ tathāgata-buddhāya svāhā. Reciting this three times while forming this mudrā, take water and bathe the Buddha.
Next, when performing the bathing ritual, remove the word *buddha* and insert the word *dharma*.
Next, at the time of bathing the Sangha, remove the character *dharma* and replace it with the character *saṃgha*.
Offer three handfuls of water to each for bathing,
having already made offerings to the Triple Gem.
When bathing the Principal Deity (Svāmin):

The Seventh Seal for Bathing the Noble Avalokiteśvara, also known as the Seal for Taking Water and Bathing One’s Own Crown with It. For this seal, both hands are turned upward with the palms side-by-side and touching each other.
The two index fingers, the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers are each extended upward,
bent, and joined together.
The two thumbs are bent and each grasps the lower part of the two index fingers.
The mantra for the mudrā is:

*Namo ratnatrayāya, namo āryavalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya tadyathā jvala mahājvala sūraprabhite svāhā*. Next, perform this mudrā and take three handfuls of water, reciting the mantra over each three times.
Having bathed the Noble Avalokiteśvara, one immediately pours [the water] over one's own crown to bathe one's body. 8.
The Seal of Self-Consecration (Ātma-abhiṣeka-mudrā), the eighth: with the two ring fingers.
With the palms facing upward, cross the right hand over the left.
Extend both little fingers straight upward with their tips touching.
Extend both middle fingers vertically and bend the first joints so that their tips touch one another.
The two index fingers each press upon the middle joint on the back of the middle fingers;
the two thumbs press upon the tips of the two ring fingers.
The mantra for this mudrā is as follows:
Oṃ hakahari hūṃ phaṭ. Having finished bathing, next perform this mudrā and mantra three times;
taking water, use it to perform self-consecration.
This dispels all those who create obstacles and difficulties. 9.
The Mudrā of Wearing Robes (Cīvaradhāraṇa-mudrā), the ninth:
With both hands, cross the thumbs over the index and middle fingers respectively.
On the small fingernail of the ring finger, the mudrā-mantra is: Oṃ vimala svāhā. With this seal:
Take water and, with the *vidyā*, sprinkle it upon one’s robes three times.
Then, with a focused mind, clearly recite over the robes three times.
Having put them on and taken them up, go to a pure place and squat facing east.
Furthermore, use soap powder and pure water to wash the hands and rinse the mouth.
The method for rinsing the mouth is as explained above and no different.
10. The *Jinding-in* (Crown-binding Seal), the tenth: Form a fist with the middle, ring, and little fingers of the right hand.
With the index finger, press against the middle joint of the thumb.
The mudrā-mantra is:
Oṃ kuru kule svāhā. Form this mudrā and recite the mantra three times, sealing it upon the crown of the head.
While performing the ritual for bathing,
one must not give rise to anger or any mind of outflows during that interval;
nor should one behold any foul or impure things, nor any groups of wicked people.
With single-minded recollection of the Noble Avalokiteśvara,
one immediately enters the maṇḍala and pays homage to the Triple Gem;
next, one pays homage to the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
Using the *saṃkṣipta-hṛdaya* (small heart mantra), recite it clearly over water five times.
Sprinkle this upon all the medicinal substances for the offerings and sprinkle it upon the maṇḍala.
11. The Eleventh: The Mudrā for Protecting the Body (*kāyarakṣā-mudrā*). Interlace the two little fingers within the palms.
Bend the two ring fingers;
press the two little fingers together with their tips crossed upward;
and extend the two middle fingers straight upward with their tips touching.
The two index fingers are slightly bent,
each positioned above the middle joint of its respective middle finger at a distance of half a finger-width.
The two thumbs are placed on the sides of the two middle fingers, palms facing upward.
The mudrā and mantra are as follows:
Oṃ vajraghoṣa-pratibodhaya svāhā. Recite this mudrā and mantra three times.
Place [the mudrā] upon the crown of the head, the two shoulders, the throat, and the heart;
this immediately constitutes the protection of the body. 12.
The Great Protection of the Body Mudrā (Mahārakṣā-mudrā), the twelfth: the characteristics of the mudrā correspond to the preceding one; the mantra is as follows:
Oṃ jvalana hūṃ phaṭ. Recite this mantra three times while forming the previously mentioned seal for protecting the body.
By touching the five places with the seal, one achieves great protection of the body.
13. The Armor Seal (Kavaca-mudrā), the thirteenth. With both hands, palms facing upward, extend all ten fingers.
The mantra for this seal is as follows:
Oṃ vidhu vidhu vikāya vidhu prajvala svāhā. Recite this seal-mantra three times while forming the seal.
From the crown of the head, touch down as far as the feet;
this constitutes the donning of the armor.
14. Illumination of the Ten Directions, Part Fourteen. Oṃ āḥ hūṃ. This mantra illuminates water and white mustard seeds.
Sprinkle and scatter [the substances] in the eight directions to bind the boundary.

15. The Mudrā for Binding the Mandala Boundary (Mandala-sīmā-bandhana-mudrā), the fifteenth: Interlace the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers within the palms, with the right hand pressing over the left.
The two index fingers are held upright and slightly askew, their tips touching one another.
The two thumbs point toward the body and the heads touch the sides;

Circumambulate the maṇḍala three times, brandishing the seal to establish the boundary of the maṇḍala. Next, [proceed] to the positions of the various holy beings within the maṇḍala.
Place it respectfully upon a vessel of fragrant water and offer flowers floating upon the water as an offering. 16.
The Sixteenth: The Mantra for Purifying the Path. OṂ (1) bhaṇami (2) bhagavati (3) mukhara mukhara (4) jayamukhara (5) svāhā (6). When one wishes to perform the invitation with this mantra:
Holding a censer, recite this seven times.
This shall open and clear the pathways and gateways in space, expel all obstacles,
and awaken the noble Avalokiteśvara and all the other holy beings.
Come and bestow your empowerment. 17.
The Seal for Invoking (Seventeenth): With the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers, the right hand presses down upon the left;

Extend the two index fingers obliquely with their tips touching.
With the two thumbs, beckon toward the tips of the two middle fingers.
When summoning, first look toward that direction.

Oṃ tūru tūru svāhā. Forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra seven times, invite all the holy ones to descend upon the site of practice.
18. The Mudrā of Welcoming (Yingyin), Number Eighteen:
With both hands, the ten fingers are interlaced with the right hand pressing over the left to form fists, with the middle joints of each finger exposed.

*Namo ratnatrayāya | namo 'rya-valokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya | padma-padma-padmapāṇe śaraṇa-śaraṇa | ehy ehi bhagavan | namo 'rya-valokiteśvarāya | ānugrahābhyudgata | āloke* | Having formed this mudrā, recite the mantra three times.

19. The Mudrā of Fragrant Water (Gandhodaka-mudrā), the nineteenth: With both hands, interlace the ten fingers with the right hand placed over the left, palms facing inward.

The mantra for this mudrā is:
Oṃ āḥ lūḥ. Recite this mantra and perform this mudrā three times.
Seal the vessel of perfumed water, hold it before your forehead, and offer it as an invitation. 20.
The Flower Seat Mudrā (Puṣpāsana-mudrā), the twenty-second: Turn the palms upward.
The two index fingers, the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers,
and the two little fingers are each held upright with their backs touching one another;
the two index fingers are each placed against the backs of the middle fingers.
The tips of the two index fingers and the upper joints of the two middle fingers are aligned.
Each of the two thumbs is placed against the lower joints of the index fingers.
The mudrā-mantra is as follows:
Oṃ padmamālāya svāhā. Having formed this mudrā and recited the mantra three times, one should arrange flower seats for all the holy ones.
He addressed him, saying, "Welcome, O Noble One!

and have thus deigned to descend to this lowly and wretched place."
"May you who possess peerless compassion grant your empowerment and accept this offering.

21. The Seal for Requesting to Sit (Āsana-nyāsa). Second and Twenty-first: With the two index fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers, cross them within the palms with the right over the left and form fists.
The two thumbs are both bent inward into the palms;
the two middle fingers are held upright with their tips touching,
moving up and down.
Next, form this mudrā and recite the heart mantra three times to invite the noble Avalokiteśvara and all the bodhisattvas,
each to take their respective seats.
Next, request the use of the Cundā-vajrī boundary-binding seal for solemn protection.
(22) The Obstacle-Removing Seal: For the twenty-second [seal], the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers, and the two little fingers [are joined].
With the palms facing inward, cross the hands so that the right hand presses upon the left.
Extend the two index fingers obliquely upward with their tips touching.
Extend the two thumbs toward the body with their tips touching.
The mudrā-mantra is:
Oṃ arya-ārya-nāga-bali-pūjāye piṇḍi svāhā. Next, perform this mudrā and recite the mantra three times.
Seal for all flower, incense, and other offering substances;
it serves to purify and remove obstacles. 23.
Offering Seal (Puṣpāñjali-mudrā), the twenty-third: join the two hands in *añjali*.
The two thumbs, the two middle fingers, the two ring fingers,
and the two little fingers have their tips each pressing the opposite side— right over left— and interlaced;

The mudrā and mantra are as follows:
Namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvānām (1) | Sarvatathāgatānām (2) | Saṃghapraveśamoha (3) | Gagana-gaṅgā (4) | Svāhā (5-6). Then, perform this mudrā and recite this mantra three times.
One should imagine making various offerings to the Noble One,
perform various praises of the Triple Gem, and offer praise to the Noble Avalokiteśvara; then,
according to one's own inclinations, make aspirations and dedicate the merit.
Repent all transgressions and resolve to attain Bodhicitta. 24.
The Mudrā for Seeking Rebirth, Number Twenty-Four: Extend the two thumbs and the two little fingers vertically with their tips touching, slightly bending them.
The two index fingers, the two middle fingers, and the two ring fingers are each held upright,
spread apart, and slightly bent,
with the tips separated by one cun (inch) from one another.
The mudrā-mantra is:
Oṃ pratimukha svāhā. Having performed this mudrā and recited this mantra three times, seal [the object] three times.
This reveals that all the Honored Ones are filled with joy;
they will protect and empower whatever blessings and aspirations are sought. 25.
The Root Mudrā: The twenty-fifth root mudrā is formed by joining the two hands in *añjali* with the palms hollowed inward.
Place the two thumbs side by side and extend them upward;
bend the two index fingers so that their tips touch the tops of the two thumbs.
Recite the Great Heart Mantra and the Small Heart Mantra.
Clearly perform the mudrā three times.
Seal the crown of the head, the left and right shoulders, the throat, and the heart.
To armor the body, seal the medicinal substances.
Recite the Great Heart Mantra and the Small Heart Mantra.
Protect with the Mantra of Light-Radiance. 26.
The Great Heart Seal (Second of the Sixteen): As before, modify the seal by placing the left hand at the heart, palm facing upward and extended.
Change the right hand so that the palm faces outward and upward;
recite the Great Heart Mantra and the Mudrā of Manifestation three times,
presenting them to the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
I pray that all activities may be accomplished. 27.
Purification of the Rosary (Akṣasūtra-śodhana-mantra). Second and Twenty-seventh. Oṃ amṛtadhāraṇi śrīye śrīmaṇi svāhā. With this mantra, purify the rosary.
One should use lotus seeds or maṇi jewels.
Bathe them with the five products of the cow.
Recite the mantra seven times over each individual jewel.
Having finished putting it on and tying it, recite the mantra one hundred and eight times clearly.
Receive and maintain it according to the ritual.
28. The Mudrā of the Rosary (Akṣamālā-mudrā), Number Twenty-Eight: With the right hand, take the rosary and place it within the palm.
Joining the two hands in *añjali*, hold the beads within the hollow of the palms and recite this mantra:
Oṃ vaśupāte śrīye pataṅga-maṇi svāhā. Recite this mantra one thousand and eight times while holding the beads clearly; thus one shall maintain it with purity.
Each time one takes up the beads, one should clearly visualize them three times.
With both hands at the level of the heart, six inches apart, or in front of the nose,
the five fingers of each hand should be held together, grasping the rosary.
As you rotate each bead, let it coincide with the light.
Sever all discursive thoughts and fix the mind single-pointedly upon the eyes,
while recollecting the syllables of the mantra of the Holy Avalokiteśvara.
The halo of light and the radiance of body and mind are like the sun, preventing any confusion.

only when the body is utterly exhausted shall the recitation and contemplation cease.
Opening his eyes, he gazed upon the holy Avalokiteśvara;
with palms joined at his crown, he prostrated and offered various praises to the holy Avalokiteśvara.

He reflected thus: "By what skillful means shall I cause all sentient beings to forever escape birth and death and realize entry into bodhi?
If one were to achieve [the power of] medicinal herbs..."
Visualize the noble Avalokiteśvara with single-minded devotion,

until the waning and waxing of the moon are completed.
As when the original medicine manifests warmth, smoke, and increased radiance, the medicine is then perfected. 29.
The Seal for Releasing the Boundary (Sīmā-bandha-mudrā). Second and Twenty-ninth: With the two ring fingers inside the palms, the right hooks over the left.
The two thumbs press upon the nails of the two ring fingers.
The two middle fingers are held upright with their tips touching one another.
The two index fingers rest against the backs of the two middle fingers, adhering to them.
Join the two little fingers together, pointing upward and touching.
The mantra is:
Oṃ hṛīḥ āḥ caṇḍamārīce hūṃ phaṭ. Having formed this mudrā, recite the mantra seven times.
Circumambulate three times to the left to dissolve the boundaries of the ritual site.
Once the boundaries have been dissolved,
again offer perfumed water as an offering and perform the rite of dismissal.
Form the mudrā for welcoming as before and sweep it outward to escort the holy ones.
30. The Thirty-first: Fivefold Purity and Radiance (Pañcaśuddhi-prabhāsvara). Oṃ 1. Yaśodhara 2. Svāhā 3. If one consumes food that has been defiled by impurities:
Using these five pure products of the bright and pure cow one hundred and eight times,
stir them together with *kuśa* grass and consume them;
this will remove all defilements caused by physical contact.
One immediately attains purity.
All medicinal substances, offering vessels,
scented water, incense, flowers, unguents, and burning incense [are likewise purified].
Whether eating, drinking, lighting lamps, grinding incense, consuming food,
putting on or taking off clothes, sprinkling water, bathing, or performing purification rites,
one should always employ a focused mind and perform each action clearly five times.
The Radiance Increases and Bestows Grace, Dispelling and Healing All Obstacles.

Even those destined for the Avīci Hell shall all be extinguished [of their karma].
Through the accomplishment of this medicinal elixir of light, merit increases and flourishes;
when seen by people, it inspires no weariness or distaste.
One shall attain great and supreme aspirations;
just as the orb of the sun dispels the darkness of the world wherever it reaches,
all cherished goals and undertakings shall be successfully accomplished.
They shall not be harmed by calamities of water or fire, nor by weapons, poisons, sorcery, or curses;
neither shall they suffer injury from tigers, wolves, or venomous insects.
Even if there should be someone facing execution, [they shall be spared].
By wearing these [substances] after fumigating them with medicinal herbs, by the power of those herbs,
the sword will immediately break into pieces and one shall attain liberation.
Furthermore, if there is someone bound in prison with cangues, fetters, stocks, or shackles, [they shall likewise be freed].
By fumigating with medicine and wearing it, one attains liberation.
When this vidyādhara performs this rite,
he should apply his mind with utmost sincerity and faith in this method, harboring no doubts.
If one practices and prepares [the medicine] according to the Dharma, it will certainly not be in vain. This medicine is poisonous;
hold it, but do not take it recklessly. Chapter Seven: The Section on Medicines from the *Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, those who possess this dhāraṇī-vidyā for the incense-manifestation are revered and cherished by all in the world."
One should take equal portions of camphor, musk, saffron, and ox-gall,
apply them to the altar to establish the boundary, and recite the mantra over the medicinal substances one thousand and eighty times; then,
mix them together and grind them into a paste.
Mix rainwater with [the powder] to form pills the size of hemp seeds.
Place them in a medicinal vessel and set it within the mandala before the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
Recite the root dhāraṇī, the great-heart mantra, and the small-heart mantra.
When performing the rite of accomplishment, wait for the moon and sun to reach their fullness;
if the medicinal substance emits warm smoke and increases its radiance, these signs are verified as successful.
Once accomplished, it should be dried in the shade in a secluded place.
If the signs of warmth appear, one should maintain the recitation and mindfulness;
all people will be gathered together, showing mutual respect and praise,
while all diseases of the mouth are completely cured and the breath becomes fragrant and pure.
If the sign of smoke appears, maintain the recitation and mindfulness;
whatever one aspires for will naturally be fulfilled,
all calamities and afflictions will be eliminated, and one's verbal karma will become pure.
If one thins out and removes defilements and obstacles, those who see them will revere and submit;
if signs of increase appear,
one will maintain the recitation and mindfulness, and their lifespan will be extended and prolonged.
When *māra* spirits and ghosts see this, they all flee in terror.
If one maintains the recitation while these radiant signs appear,
one will realize the stage of a supernaturally enlightened immortal (*vidyādhara*) and attain the wisdom that knows past lives.
The five sins of immediate retribution will naturally be extinguished;
all worldly calamities will be liberated from.
Kings, princes, queens, and court ladies [shall likewise be freed].
Ministers, officials, the populace, and followers of external paths— upon seeing, hearing,
or discussing these various words, they all believe and accept them,
listening with joy, and they submit themselves, making offerings and serving him.
By bestowing all manner of wealth and treasures, everything is accomplished;
like the Cakravartin King Mandhātṛ who nurtured the world with compassion,
one attains the privilege of sitting upon the same throne as Śakra.
By possessing this power of the medicinal herbs,
the vidyādhara shall never forget anything he hears or retains;
his worldly wisdom and eloquence shall be unimpeded.
His speech and voice will be harmonious and elegant, like that of a *kiṃnara*, causing all who hear it to rejoice.
If one holds this medicine while entering the fray of battle, one will certainly defeat the enemy army.
If one constantly holds the medicine and recites the mantra according to the ritual, [the same result shall follow].
The Noble Avalokiteśvara will appear before this person and fulfill their requested aspirations according to their heart's desire.
Furthermore, there is a method: construct a maṇḍala measuring four cubits.
The base is two chi high, leveled, smoothed, and wiped clean;
it is plastered with cow dung and yellow earth, and smeared with white sandalwood paste.
Upon the altar, place an image of the Holy Avalokiteśvara.
The image should face west.
One should offer incense, flowers, and lamps at the three times of day,
with the sole exception of bitter flowers and foul-smelling flowers.
One should offer incense by burning agallochum and white sandalwood.
One should fashion a *maṇi*-banner from white sandalwood wood, one cubit in height;
the top of the banner is adorned with silken fabrics, from which streamers hang down.
Atop the banner-head is placed a maṇi jewel;
this jewel is made of red crystal or rock crystal,
both pure and free from any flaw or blemish.
Place the banner upon the center of the altar.
Suspend seven medicinal pills from the top of the banner.
To the west of the altar, perform the ritual while seated cross-legged, facing east.
Recite the root dhāraṇī, the Great Heart Mantra, and the Small Heart Mantra,
and invoke the noble Avalokiteśvara,
Śakra Devendra, Mahābrahmā, and the Four Heavenly Kings.
The Vidyādhara Śivamāha Vidyārāja,
the One-Tufted Rākṣasī, and the Dūtī messenger—
recite these separately one thousand and eighty times each.
One should make offerings by burning incense, scattering flowers, and praising with a Brahma-voice for a full hundred days and nights;
thus, one’s requests before the noble Avalokiteśvara will be fulfilled according to one's wishes.
All shall be subdued and brought into compliance, abiding in peace;
one shall attain the ability to travel together with the mantra-siddhas,
and all sages shall respect and protect one due to these karmic conditions.
Until the end of life, you must request that he go to the place where the messenger is stationed; do not doubt this at all.
This is called the method of the Wish-Fulfilling Secret Messenger.
As for those who employ the medicinal substances:
One should grind medicinal pills according to the number of days [required] into a powder,
mix it with rock honey to form pills, and place them in a silver vessel.
Recite the Great Heart Mantra and the Small Heart Mantra one thousand and eighty times.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times while holding the medicine and touching it to the two feet of the Bodhisattva.
Place it in a secret and pure location.
Whenever you wish to take it orally, recite the mantra twenty-one times.
If one silently recites the Threefold Veda (Trividyā) one hundred and eight times while maintaining internal retention,
all spirits and ghosts who are difficult to subdue will be brought under control;
they will obey one's will and be dispatched as required, swiftly accomplishing all tasks.
Whether held or worn, wherever one goes,
all who see it will rejoice and none will fail to harmonize with them;
one will be able to accomplish all secret and wondrous deeds.
Whether entering a royal palace, entering a monastic assembly,
entering a village, or entering among non-Buddhists,
one should always secretly contain the medicine within and silently recite the vidyā-mantra.
By gathering the characteristics of wholesome speech and instruction,
one attains all signs of compliance, submission, and mutual harmony,
and whatever the mind contemplates and seeks shall be fully accomplished.
One will always receive the love, respect, and offerings of noble persons.
If one constantly practices this Dharma in accordance with the Dharma,
one should receive various kinds of sublime offerings day after day.
If one encounters hostile armies or engages in conflict,
one shall achieve victory in all such battles. For this reason,
the Noble Avalokiteśvara protects [the practitioner] at all times like a beloved son, bestowing great sovereignty.
For one who performs this rite, it excludes those who lack a sincere heart.
Chapter Eight: The Section on Eye Medicines from the *Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
He addressed the Buddha again, saying: "World-Honored One,
this dhāraṇī and the method for the eye-ointment of clear vision cause all sentient beings to obtain great benefits and achieve their wishes."
May the Noble Avalokiteśvara fulfill all requested aspirations. As for the medicinal ingredients:

take equal parts of realgar (*manaḥśilā*) and *kākapuṣpī* (which the Tang translation identifies as the seeds of *Cirsium arvense*; the original translation states to take the seeds of *Cirsium arvense* and the filaments of the red lotus). Burn these to collect the liquid residue.

Blue lotus petals, ox-gallstone (*gorocanā*), saffron, *kuṅkuma*, and *yuhui*—in other versions this is translated as dried ginger, though its identity remains uncertain; one source calls it elephant bile; two sources list small juniper and *pippalī*; long pepper; and sea foam.
Recite the mantra for the consecration of the altar and the boundary-delineation one thousand and eighty times over medicinal herbs;
then blend and grind them together.
Furthermore, add musk, camphor, and naturally occurring rock honey.
Reduce each of the aforementioned medicines by half, blend them together, and grind them finely.
Place them in a copper vessel and set it within the mandala before the Noble Avalokiteśvara.
Recite the root mantra, the great-heart mantra, and the small-heart mantra.
When performing the rite of accomplishment (*sādhana*), one should wait for the moon and sun to reach their fullness and perfection.
When the medicine emits warmth, smoke, and radiant light,
the medicine is then accomplished.
According to the signs of accomplishment and realization— whether superior, middling,
or inferior— one should first smear medicine upon the feet of the Noble Avalokiteśvara and arouse great compassion for all sentient beings.
When reciting the first three mantras one hundred and eight times, one should apply them to the eyes;
all obscurations, white halos, rheum, tears,
red membranes, night-blindness, fetal redness, and wind-induced redness shall be removed.
Any protruding flesh in the eyes shall be completely cured.
For those who apply it a second time, all headaches,
or pain in half the head, or various diseases of the mouth shall be healed.
Feverish illnesses that manifest on the first day, second day, or third day,
or those that manifest constantly, shall all be completely cured.
This applies to those who apply [the ointment] for the third time.
All evil spirits, diseases of the gods, diseases of demons, epilepsy, and wind disorders—
even the eighty-four thousand various types of afflictions caused by spirits and ghosts—
shall all be completely cured.
As for the fourth application:
all obstructing Vināyakas, as well as various demons,
ghosts, and spirits, shall be terrified and depart far away.
As for the fifth application:
one will achieve victory over all enemies, calamities, military arrays,
and conflicts, and shall possess great majestic power.
As for the sixth application:
all grave offenses, including the five deeds of immediate retribution (*ānantarya-karma*),
which would otherwise lead one to fall into the Avīci Hell— [are purified by this].
Furthermore, all evil dreams, calamities, portents,
and inauspicious signs shall be entirely extinguished.
This is the seventh application of the ointment.
The king, princes, queens, concubines, ministers, officials, and subordinates— all men and women alike—
completely followed his lead, placing their faith in him,
turning toward him with affection and joy, and making offerings to him.
One who anoints [the body] for the second seven-day period attains great sovereignty.
One who anoints it for the third seven-day period plants merit like that of a king;
all the people will submit to, follow, draw near to, and make offerings to them.
As for the fourth application, performed seven times:
all yakṣas and yakṣiṇīs, along with their kinsmen and retinues,
will be subdued at will and serve as one's attendants.
Fifth, those who apply it seven times [will be protected from] all rākṣasas and rākṣasīs,
as well as all asuras and asurīs.
All nāgas and nāga maidens will be brought under his control and made to serve him as attendants.
As for the sixth and seventh applications [of the ointment]:
All the mighty ḍākinīs and yoginīs who fly through the air by means of illusory transformations manifest in various forms to serve at will according to one's intent.
They shall follow and protect [the practitioner] until they attain enlightenment.
For those who apply [this ointment] seven times on the seventh day,
the Mahākāla spirits, the Mother of Ghosts (Hārītī), and the deities of the eight classes [shall likewise provide protection].
They will all be subdued, follow [the practitioner], and provide protection.
One who applies it seven times for the eighth time will be able to see all the invisible classes of sages (ṛṣis).
The ninth time of application, performed seven times,
enables one to see all hidden treasures within the earth.
The seventeenth time of application—
One is able to see all the palaces of the sages and the palaces of the asuras with all their gates open,
and one sees everyone entering and exiting within those palaces.
This is the eleventh time of anointing seven times.
Entering the mountain forests, one is able to see all the essences of medicinal herbs manifesting their forms.
Their majestic radiance is brilliant; by seeking them, one attains longevity and great power, gathering them as one desires.
The twelfth application, performed seven times,
can open the gates of the palaces of the mountain deities and ṛṣis;
therein, the deities and ṛṣis will welcome the vidyādhara.
If one enters [the ocean] with this elixir of the immortals, one’s wishes will be fulfilled.
Thirteen times, when applied sevenfold,
it can open all the dragon palaces within the sea.
Seeing this, the assembly of nāgas all rejoice without hindrance.
As for the fourteenth application of the ointment seven times:
one is able to see all the palace chambers of the deities in the desire realm, with every door opened.
The fifteenth application of the ointment is that one travels at night through pitch darkness and sees as clearly as by day.
The sixteenth application of the ointment is...
One who can see the limits of water, the adamantine limit, the limit of the wind-circle, and the limit of space;
one who applies [the ointment] seventeen times for the seventeenth application,
can see the Heaven of the Four Great Kings.
Furthermore, one is able to look down upon sentient beings suffering in the hells and cause all those beings to attain liberation.
This is the eighteenth [practice]: applying [the ointment] seven times.
His majestic radiance is like the sun that destroys all darkness.
The nineteenth [application], when smeared seven times,
enables one to see the noble Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva.
May all aspirations be fulfilled.
Regarding the twenty-seventh application of ointment:
one will be able to see the noble Avalokiteśvara, and all sought-after aspirations will be fully satisfied.

Twenty-first: One who applies [the ointment] seven times will be able to attain supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) and behold the palaces of the devas in the realm of form (*rūpadhātu*), moving through them with sovereign ease and without obstruction.
Furthermore, they will see all the oceans of lands in the ten directions, including the assemblies of Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Pratyekabuddhas, and Śrāvakas, as well as the pure Buddha-fields.
If one applies [the ointment] for one year,
by secretly upholding the Three Vidyās, one will attain the pure Five Eyes,
as well as a mass of merit and virtue, supernatural powers, and majestic might.
It will further increase until it equals that of the gods.
Whenever applying the medicinal ointment, dip a copper spoon into the medicine and apply it clearly twenty-one times;
dot it onto the eyes while maintaining the vidyā-mantra according to the ritual rules.
If any sentient beings practice this dharma seeking supreme vows,
they should have deep faith and understanding, giving rise to no doubt or hesitation;
they should constantly give rise to great compassion for all sentient beings and study the wisdom of the Buddha.
One will immediately achieve success as previously described;
all undertakings will certainly not be in vain.
However, if the practitioner conceives doubts in their mind and does not apply themselves with single-minded diligence, [success will not be attained].
All dharmas that have been performed will not be accomplished.
Chapter Nine: The Homavidhi of the Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī Sūtra. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
He addressed the Buddha again, saying: "World-Honored One,
this dhāraṇī is the vidyā-homa rite that benefits sentient beings and accomplishes all most supreme dharmas."
It destroys all veils and obstructions and subdues all enemies.
No *vināyakas* shall obstruct or afflict them.
All people who see it will rejoice.
In a clean place, measure out a space of three cubits and prepare the ground by smearing it.
In the center, dig a circular fire-pit one cubit in diameter and half a cubit deep.
Then, smear and polish it according to the ritual rules using cow dung and yellow clay.
Take white sandalwood two and a half spans long;
cut it into pieces and pile them in the incense burner to burn.
Divide these equally with rice-pollen, white mustard seeds, and *śrīkhaṇḍa* (aquatic) incense, then mix them with clarified butter, honey, milk, and curd.
If one performs one thousand and eighty *homa* offerings at the fifth watch of the night,
the five sins of immediate retribution and all karmic obstructions will be extinguished simultaneously.
If one performs the *homa* for seven days, [the same result shall be attained].
One’s lifespan shall not be cut short, one shall be delivered from all grave sins, and one shall attain purity of body.
If one performs homa for two weeks,
merit and longevity will increase, surpassing even those of kings, princes, ministers, and the common people.
If one performs homa for twenty-one days while being regarded with love and reverence as if serving the god Agni,
Śakra Devānām Indra of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven [will appear].
Together with the hosts of devas and the Sun and Moon Devas,
they all come to provide protection and fulfill all aspirations.
The divine kings of the Four Great Kings, the vidyādhara sages, and their retinues likewise do so.
All shall come to provide protection and manifest their efficacy.
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, Mahāpraṇidhāna,
and the Noble Avalokiteśvara shall each manifest their bodies.
He shall be granted great vows that are fulfilled according to his wishes,
causing all the people of the world to revere and submit to him.
If there is a drought among the heavens, one should mix white mustard seeds with ghee.
If one performs *homa* according to the ritual for three days and three nights, a sweet rain will descend.
If there is excessive rain, take the *homa* ashes and gaze upward into the sky while reciting [the mantra] one hundred and eight times clearly.
If one scatters [the ashes] into the air above, the rain will immediately clear.
If calamitous winds, hail, or rain should suddenly arise,
perform a homa with the ashes while reciting the mantra one hundred and eight times.
When one looks toward it, the wind and hail will immediately cease.
If one constantly recites the vidyā-mantra according to the Dharma,
one’s majestic power and spiritual efficacy will be such that there is nothing to fear, like that of Nārāyaṇa.
Upon casting off this body, one will be reborn immediately in the Western World of Ultimate Bliss.
In whatever place one is born, one will constantly remember past lives;
until reaching Bodhi, one shall not fall into the evil realms.
World-Honored One, this vidyā-mantra of the *Cintāmaṇicakra-dhāraṇī* possesses immeasurable merit that exceeds the ocean and is boundless.
Whether it be bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or boys and girls—
Those who can rely on this Dharma without giving rise to doubt or confusion,
and who constantly transcribe, read, recite, and uphold it,
will have their minds retain all matters of activity.
They all attained great majestic power according to their wishes.
At that time, the fourfold assembly of faithful men and women all came to love and revere them,
and the King of Vidyādharas, together with the host of ṛṣis, protected them in secret and in silence.
Furthermore, auspicious and meritorious deeds will be spontaneously accomplished;
one will attain great nobility, reverence, and offerings,
as well as all manner of wealth, jewels, pearls, and mani-gems.
Gold, silver, lapis lazuli, conch shells, jade discs, and precious gems,
as well as clothing and musical instruments, were all abundant;
for they had attained great merit and fulfilled their various aspirations.
When this vidyādhara attains this auspicious siddhi of the wish-fulfilling wheel, they must not lightly disclose it to others;
the supernatural powers thus obtained will never decline or be lost.
World-Honored One, this is the mantra, mudrā, and vidyā of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel Dhāraṇī.
Such majestic power is truly rare and marvelous.
Whether pure or impure, it can bring sentient beings to completion;
the mind is tranquil within the ocean of Dharma as it enters all samādhis.
Dwelling in the playful sport of the divine way, I abide in the bodhi of the Buddha.
By these causes and conditions, I bring sentient beings to maturity through great compassion;
I only pray for the Tathāgata’s empowerment and protection.
10. Chapter on the Entrustment. The *Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, Chapter Ten: The Entrustment. At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
Excellent, excellent, O Great Compassionate One!
You have skillfully expounded this vidyā-mantra of the Cintāmaṇicakra Dhāraṇī.
This dharma [shall flourish] in Jambudvīpa.
The roots of virtue of bodhicitta that bring about the maturation, benefit, and happiness of all sentient beings—
if there are any sentient beings who resolve their minds upon this *vidyā* of the *Cintāmaṇicakra-dhāraṇī*, [they shall attain these benefits].
For one who constantly recites, studies, and upholds [this teaching] without interruption,
within this very life,
they shall realize and behold the samādhi of the wisdom that witnesses the quiescence of form and sports with the supernatural powers of perfect illumination.
Not only will one obtain great benefit and fortune in the present life,
but one will also acquire great merit in future births.
For this reason, all the devas, nāgas, and the eight classes of beings...
All should honor and protect them as one would serve the Fire God.
I entrust these holders of the vidyā-mantra to you;
always exert yourself to guard them with diligence.
Those who contemplate this clarity shall obtain its verification;
seeing and believing in you, my body, I rejoice.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—
He addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One,
throughout immeasurable kalpas, by the power of great compassion,
I have received the Tathāgata’s teaching and been entrusted with sentient beings."
They shall constantly follow, protect, and grant their efficacy;
may the Buddha himself bear witness to this,
as I now proclaim for the sake of sentient beings this *Rucigartā-dhāraṇī-vidyā*.
If those who uphold [this] practice it according to their recitations,
their vows will be fulfilled and its realization will not be difficult;
by virtue of the Buddha’s spiritual power, they shall be able to thus rescue sentient beings from suffering.
At that time, when the Holy Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara had finished speaking this sutra, the entire great assembly was filled with great joy;
they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
*The Sutra of the Wish-Fulfilling Wheel Dhāraṇī*.
